rendered: The carbon micropores are about ∼0.5 nm[1] across, measured by FFT of TEM images. The solvent molecule is larger, at about ∼0.7 nm in diameter[2], so the pores are too small to accommodate it. The sodium ion is much smaller, at about ∼0.2 nm in diameter[3]. So the ion must shed its solvent shell at the surface of the microporous host and then move on alone to the sulfur, where it reacts in a forming a quasi solid-state reaction[4] rather than in the solution-based conversion of a typical battery.
